mechanism_narrative: IGF1R (RTK) and OSMR (cytokine receptor) are co-expressed in aged skeletal muscle (MuSC, FB, MF-I/II). The flexible_GS4 linker (~20 Å) forces close proximity between IGF1R's kinase domain (residues 999-1274) and OSMR's JAK-docked intracellular domain. IGF1R transphosphorylates OSMR's juxtamembrane tyrosines, enabling GRB2-SHC1-RAS-MAPK and IRS1-PI3K-AKT signaling, while OSMR-recruited JAK1/2 transphosphorylate IGF1R, enabling STAT3 activation. PLCG1/2 are sterically excluded due to the short linker geometry and large ECD asymmetry (IGF1R ECD=195aa vs OSMR ECD=713aa, ratio 3.66×), which orients the kinase domains at an angle incompatible with PLCγ docking. The biased output is MAPK+AKT+STAT3 activation without PLCγ/Ca²⁺ signaling, producing a muscle structural gene program (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, TAGLN) and suppressing aged IEG markers (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32, TXNIP).
